powershell.title: PowerShell 7
powershell.question: Run the command in PowerShell. What did the result look like?

options.label: A single line, for example PowerShell 7.6.0
options.explanation: PowerShell 7 is installed and works. From now on, always use this program.

options.label: An error message that says “not recognized”
options.explanation: PowerShell 7 wasn’t found. Either the installation isn’t finished yet, or the terminal needs to be restarted.

options.label: I opened a program called Windows PowerShell
options.explanation: That’s the old PowerShell 5.1. PowerShell 7 is a different program, and you’ll find it in the Start menu under the name PowerShell 7.

options.label: Something else
options.explanation: No worries, let’s figure it out together.

git.title: Git
git.question: Run the command in the terminal. What did the result look like?

options.label: git version and a number, for example git version 2.56.0
options.explanation: Git is installed. The exact number may be different, and that’s completely fine.

label.windows: An error message that says “not recognized”

options.explanation: The terminal can’t find Git. Most of the time, closing the terminal and opening it again helps.

label.mac: A window popped up about installing the command line developer tools

options.explanation: The installation isn’t finished yet. See troubleshooting for how to continue.

options.label: Something else
options.explanation: No worries, let’s figure it out together.

vscode.title: VS Code
vscode.question: Run the command in the terminal. What did the result look like?

options.label: Three lines: a version number, a long string of letters and numbers, and x64 or arm64
options.explanation: VS Code is installed, and the terminal can find it. You can open folders with the command code .

options.label: An error message: command not found
options.explanation: VS Code may be installed, but the terminal can’t find the code command yet.

options.label: Something else
options.explanation: No worries, let’s figure it out together.

gh.title: GitHub CLI
gh.question: Run the command in the terminal. What did the result look like?

options.label: gh version, a number and a date, plus a link
options.explanation: GitHub CLI is installed. Next, you’ll sign in.

options.label: An error message: command not found
options.explanation: The terminal can’t find the gh command. Restart the terminal, and it will most likely be fixed.
A tool needed for the installation is missing. Troubleshooting has instructions for installing it.

options.label: Something else
options.explanation: No worries, let’s figure it out together.

claude.title: Claude Code
claude.question: Run the command in a new terminal window. What did the result look like?

options.label: A version number followed by (Claude Code)
options.explanation: Claude Code is installed! Next, you’ll sign in.

options.label: An error message: command not found
options.explanation: The terminal can’t find the claude command. Open a new terminal window and try again.

label.windows: An error that says “running scripts is disabled”
label.mac: The installation stopped with an error

options.explanation: The installation didn’t go through. Troubleshooting has instructions.

options.label: Something else
options.explanation: No worries, let’s figure it out together.

claude-sovellus.title: Claude desktop app
claude-sovellus.question: Start Claude. What do you see?

options.label: A sign-in window or, if you’re already signed in, Claude’s start screen
options.explanation: The app is installed! Next, you’ll sign in and open the Code tab.

options.label: A blank or frozen window
options.explanation: The app started, but something didn’t finish. Troubleshooting has instructions.

options.label: I can’t find the app after installing it
options.explanation: No worries, the app has most likely been installed, or the installation didn’t finish. Troubleshooting tells you where to look.

options.label: Something else
options.explanation: No worries, let’s figure it out together.

code-valilehti.title: Code tab
code-valilehti.question: Click Code at the top of the sidebar. What do you see?

options.label: A text box with a row of options below it
options.explanation: The Code tab works! You’re ready to give Claude its first task.

options.label: A prompt to upgrade your plan
options.explanation: Your account doesn’t have a plan that includes Claude Code, or you’re signed in with a different account.

options.label: A 403 error or another sign-in error
options.explanation: Something is wrong with signing in. Usually signing in again helps.

options.label: Something else
options.explanation: No worries, let’s figure it out together.
